what: How a MRMhubExperiment object is used in a workflow
title: MRMhub overview
text: MRMhubExperiment object created start workflow. Data metadata imported , used subsequent processing, plotting, reporting steps. mrmhub function takes MRMhubExperiment object first argument, processing functions return updated MRMhubExperiment object. returned object typically assigned back name, passed next function. Plotting functions instead return plot (typically ggplot2 object). MRMhubExperiment objects can also used native R pipe (|>), forwards object one function next.
code: mexp <- MRMhubExperiment() mexp <- import_data_mrmhub(mexp, path = "data/results.tsv") mexp <- normalize_by_istd(mexp)  # equivalently, chained with the R pipe: mexp <- MRMhubExperiment() |>   import_data_mrmhub(path = "data/results.tsv") |>   normalize_by_istd()

title: MRMhub overview
text: MRMhub’s public functions fall four groups, names follow consistent convention: Data exchange — read measured data metadata object, write results (tables, plots, reports) back disk. Data processing — transforms normalize, correct (drift, batch, isotopic interference), quantify measurements, compute per-feature QC metrics. QC charts — return plots visual inspection run order, normalization, corrections, calibration, sample relationships. QC filtering — apply pass/fail thresholds features exclude features analyses fail QC. functions arranged pipeline stage, see Function map. Function reference lists every function full parameter detail.

title: Design decisions behind MRMhub QUANT
text: canonical exchange format INTEGRATOR QUANT long CSV one row per feature per sample. Long format handles variable number features per study without NA padding, straightforward filter, group, join, feeds directly ggplot2 without intermediate pivot. also keeps distinction missing value true zero explicit.

what: Feature and analyte as distinct identifiers
title: Design decisions behind MRMhub QUANT
text: feature_id identifies distinct signal extracted MS data; analyte_id identifies compound signal measures. two kept separate one--one. One analyte can produce several features (isotopes, adducts, transitions), one feature can carry several analytes isobaric isomeric, SM PC species. INTEGRATOR selects one quantifier signal per feature, time data reaches QUANT feature_id holds one value per sample, analyte_id links features measure compound.

title: Design decisions behind MRMhub QUANT
text: dataset_orig never modified import; processing operates dataset. Keeping imported data untouched means step can re-run without re-importing, processed values can compared originals verify correction, raw data remains available review point.
code: # You can always reset: mexp@dataset <- mexp@dataset_orig  # Or compare before/after: original <- mexp@dataset_orig |> dplyr::filter(feature_id == "LPC_18:1") processed <- mexp@dataset |> dplyr::filter(feature_id == "LPC_18:1")

title: Design decisions behind MRMhub QUANT
text: Drift batch corrections typically fitted QC samples; gaussian-kernel method exception, fitting study samples large, well-randomised cohorts. Reference: Broadhurst et al. (2018). Metabolomics, 14, 72. Fitting study samples remove real biological variation together analytical trend, external reference alone always available responds poorly within-run drift. Fitting QC samples therefore requires enough per batch (rule thumb least five, evenly distributed across run) correction stable.

what: Processing order by convention, not enforcement
title: Design decisions behind MRMhub QUANT
text: Functions intended called set order, package signals order status flags rather enforcing hard errors. Strict enforcement avoided valid workflows legitimately skip steps: assay without internal standards omits normalization, short single-batch run needs drift correction. Hard errors obstruct exploratory reprocessing. status flags record run let function warn prerequisite missing, without blocking.
code: # Recommended order: # 1. import # 2. add_metadata # 3. set_analysis_order # 4. normalize_by_istd # 5. correct_drift_* # 6. correct_batch_* # 7. quantify_by_* # 8. calc_qc_metrics # 9. filter_features_qc

title: Drift and batch correction
text: following drift correction methods available MRMhub, two typically used QC samples one (gaussian kernel-based) study samples. Corrections can applied batch--batch basis (batch_wise = TRUE, default) across batches (batch_wise = FALSE). correction can either replace existing drift batch corrections (replace_previous = TRUE, default) applied top existing corrections (replace_previous = FALSE). Drift correction can applied features (conditional_correction = FALSE) conditionally, based whether sample CV difference correction defined threshold (cv_diff_threshold). conditional correction applied separately batch batch_wise = TRUE. recommended visually inspect correction using plot_runscatter() function. Set argument recalc_trend_after = TRUE trends correction also available plotting. details, refer description plot_runscatter(). , however, doubles processing time. function outputs message indicating median CV change mean absolute CV correction samples. However, metrics experimental used definitive criteria correction (see function documentation). cubic spline smoothing approach, particularly used regularization parameter lambda, similar identical previously described QC-based drift correction methods, QC-RSC (Quality Control Regularized Spline Correction), described Dunn et al. (2011) Kirwan et al. (2013). See tutorial Drift batch correction information use functions plot results.

title: Drift and batch correction
text: MRMhub provides three batch-correction methods. Batch correction applied normalization , used, drift correction. Median centering (correct_batch_centering()) aligns per-batch medians selected QC types (ref_qc_types), following QC-based paradigm (Broadhurst et al. 2018); scale batches can optionally also equalized. default, robust choice. ComBat (correct_batch_combat()) applies empirical-Bayes location scale model Johnson et al. (2007), shrinking batch estimates across features. Unlike two methods, ComBat estimates batch effects samples rather reference QCs; supply covariates protect biological signal unbalanced designs. SERRF (correct_batch_serrf()) removes systematic error per-feature random forests trained reference QCs, using feature’s correlated features predictors (Fan et al. 2019). captures non-linear batch drift effects jointly best suited larger panels dense QC coverage. correct_batch_combat() correct_batch_serrf() experimental. ComBat requires optional sva package SERRF optional ranger package. SERRF implementation adapts reference code malbacR package (Leach et al. 2023); validate results reference implementation data. See tutorial Drift batch correction information.

text: Q: importer use? : See Import prepare data files decision flowchart matching vendor/file layout importer. Q: import_data_masshunter() aborts “Data file unsupported corrupted format…”. : Almost always wrong importer file — plain, Skyline, INTEGRATOR CSV passed MassHunter parser. Use importer matches file’s format. file really MassHunter export, re-export MH Quant compounds columns. Q: “file read single column using ‘,’ delimiter.” : file semicolon- tab-delimited (common European Excel locales), comma reader sees one column. Re-export CSV UTF-8 (Comma delimited) re-import. Q: “Imported data measures feature analysis.” : Read values message. Identical values mean data read twice (result file, overlapping part ). Differing values mean two real measurements carry IDs: two injections sharing raw_data_filename (default analysis_id), wrong column mapped analysis_id/feature_id. Q: wide CSV aborts “columns feature values must numeric.” : Metadata columns mixed feature block. Point first_feature_column first real feature column, pass na_strings text missing-value tokens. Q: Skyline import aborts “Molecule Name unique identifier transition.” : Several transitions share molecule name. Build unique IDs precursor/product names masses. Q: Feature names data don’t match feature annotation. : Trailing whitespace case differences ("Compound " vs "Compound ") break join. Compare directions:

text: Q: “None analyses data match imported analysis metadata.” : Either wrong metadata file, analysis_ids formatted differently two sources. Import strips raw-file extensions squishes whitespace, residual mismatch means IDs genuinely differ — compare setdiff() . Q: “analyses data corresponding metadata.” : analyses row analysis metadata. Add missing rows, import excl_unmatched_analyses = TRUE drop unannotated analyses. Q: metadata import aborts validation warnings. : validation report printed, “Please verify warnings corresponding metadata. Use ignore_warnings = TRUE ignore warnings.” Fix flagged issues, re-import ignore_warnings = TRUE. hard “Metadata validation failed — see report .” (duplicate IDs, missing mandatory values) bypassed must corrected.

title: Troubleshooting and FAQ
text: Q: Normalised intensities come back NA. : normalize_by_istd() aborts default feature internal standard assigned (“…ISTD defined…”), feature carries istd_feature_id (“ISTDs defined feature metadata.”). Find unassigned features, assign istd_feature_id — pass ignore_missing_annotation = TRUE set NA continue. Q: “Data needs ISTD normalized, please run ‘normalize_by_istd’ first.” : Quantitation drift/batch correction normalised concentration variables run normalisation. Run normalize_by_istd() quantify_by_istd() quantify_by_calibration(). Q: “Acquisition timestamps present analysis results.” : vendor export carries acquisition time, set_analysis_order() order "timestamp". Order result-file name column metadata instead. Q: Drift batch correction aborts “One specified qc_types present dataset.” : reference QC label matching rows — misspelled QC type, QC samples run, add_metadata() run qc_type still empty. Drift batch correction fit QC samples , valid QC type must present. Q: Correction fails “Normalized intensities available” “Concentration data available”. : asked correct variable produced yet. Run upstream step first (normalize_by_istd(), quantify_*()), correct variable = "intensity". Q: “Batch correction applied one batch.” : -batch correction needs one batch_id. single batch nothing centre — skip run rest pipeline normally. Q: Drift correction makes data worse. : Loess fitting needs enough evenly-spaced QC samples per batch; , QC trend flat (noise, drift), fit can add variance. Inspect QC trend correcting, skip drift correction batches flat.

Adjust the file #> paths and parameters below, then run each chunk. #>  #> New to MRMhub? See the [MRMhub documentation](https://slinghub.github.io/MRMhub/quant/). #>  #> ```{r} #> #| label: setup #> #| include: false #> library(mrmhub) #> # Render mrmhub's coloured console feedback in HTML output: #> mrmhub_enable_cli_color() #> ``` #>  #> ## Import data #>  #> Create the experiment container and import the raw results. #>  #> ```{r} #> #| label: import-data #> mexp <- MRMhubExperiment() #> mexp <- import_data_mrmhub(mexp, path = "MRMhub_demo.tsv", import_metadata = TRUE) #> ``` #>  #> ## Normalize by internal standard #>  #> Divide each feature by its assigned internal standard to correct for extraction and injection variability. #>  #> ```{r} #> #| label: normalize-istd #> mexp <- normalize_by_istd(mexp) #> ``` #>  #> ## Quantify against internal-standard concentrations #>  #> Convert normalized signals to concentrations using the spiked internal-standard amounts. #>  #> ```{r} #> #| label: quantify-istd #> mexp <- quantify_by_istd(mexp) #> ``` #>  #> ## Export results #>  #> Write the processed results to an Excel report. #>  #> ```{r} #> #| label: export #> # Written next to this .qmd -- change the path or file name if you like. #> save_report_xlsx(mexp, path = "results.xlsx") #> ```

title: Get calibration metrics — get_calibration_metrics
text: feature_id: Feature identifier. is_quantifier: Logical, indicates feature quantifier. fit_model: Regression model used fitting. fit_weighting: Weighting method used fitting. lowest_cal: Lowest nonzero calibration concentration. highest_cal: Highest calibration concentration. r2: R² value, indicating goodness fit. weighted fit weighted coefficient determination (computed weighted sums squares), matching value reported vendor software Agilent MassHunter weighted curve. coef_a: Intercept (0th-order term, x^0) fitted curve. coef_b: 1st-order (linear, x^1) coefficient — slope linear fit, linear term quadratic fit. coef_c: 2nd-order (quadratic, x^2) coefficient quadratic fits. Returns NA linear fits. sigma: Standard deviation residuals. reg_failed: TRUE regression fitting failed. LoD = 3.3× sample standard error residuals / slope regression (see Notes). LoQ = 10× sample standard error residuals / slope regression (see Notes). coefficients describe curve ascending power order (R's lm() / poly() convention): response = coef_a + coef_b * x + coef_c * x^2. reverse descending *x^2 + b*x + c form used vendor software (e.g. Agilent MassHunter, x^2 term), comparing export, match power, letter. Note: LoD/LoQ follow ICH Q2(R1/R2) approach (3.3 sigma / S 10 sigma / S). slope S slope calibration curve zero concentration (linear coefficient coef_b); quadratic fit quadratic term contribute slope. response sigma selectable calc_calibration_results() via lod_sigma (residual standard error, default, standard error intercept); sigma column reported always residual standard error. weighted fit (1/x, 1/x^2, 1/sqrt(x)) sigma R's weighted residual standard error, raw response scale ICH 3.3 sigma / S formula assumes, reported LoD/LoQ approximate (typically slightly optimistic 1/x). Use fit_weighting = "none" require strict ICH response-scale Sy/x; back-calculated concentrations unaffected.

title: mrmhub 0.9.9 (development)
text: Considerably enhanced console output error messages: clearer, actionable messages, -front argument validation, truthful processing summaries make step easier follow debug. Substantially improved data metadata import: robust sample feature ID normalization matching, deduplication, stronger schema validation greatly reduce silent input errors. Consistent, configurable plotting: shared appearance arguments (font sizes, colours, legend placement sizing) refined house theme, now settable globally via mrmhub_set_plot_defaults(). Flexible figure export: new save_plot() writes plot_*() figure file defined physical size format, including multi-page PDFs, paged plot functions gain configurable page dimensions. MS1 MS2 (MRM) isotope interference correction: full correction engine precursor (MS1) transition-level (MRM) isotopic interferences, MRM patterns based LICAR method (Gao et al., Anal. Chem., 2021). New batch-correction methods (experimental): empirical-Bayes ComBat (correct_batch_combat(), Johnson et al. 2007) SERRF random-forest normalization (correct_batch_serrf(), Fan et al. 2019), complementing existing correct_batch_centering(). Export SummarizedExperiment LipidomicsExperiment: results convert directly Bioconductor SummarizedExperiment lipidr LipidomicsExperiment objects downstream analysis. Save, share, reload complete experiments: save_dataset_rds() read_dataset_rds() serialize whole MRMhubExperiment single, self-contained .rds file, making complete datasets easy archive share; content hash embedded save verified load. new features: mzTab-M import export, status dashboard (mrmhub_status()) compact object printing quick overview. Improved robustness, speed, stability: better handling missing values analytical-sequence gaps, faster QC-metric computation, many bug fixes based user feedback. Fully revised documentation: rewritten, task-oriented site tutorials, manual, recipes.
